en: Dhātukathā 2 Niddesa 2.11.
The Eleventh Method: Exposition of the Terms "Associated" and "Dissociated" by Way of Comprehension.
Regarding those phenomena included by the truth of the origin,

and those phenomena included by the truth of the path— whether by way of inclusion in the aggregates, inclusion in the bases, or inclusion in the elements— with how many aggregates, with how many bases, and with how many elements are those phenomena associated?
Those phenomena are associated with three aggregates, with one base, and with seven elements.
They are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
With one base (āyatana) and with one element (dhātu), they are dissociated from some [factors].

As for those factors associated with the female faculty (itthindriya) … and those factors associated with the male faculty (purisindriya) which are included in the aggregate-inclusion (khandha-saṅgaha), the base-inclusion (āyatana-saṅgaha), and the element-inclusion (dhātu-saṅgaha): with how many aggregates, with how many bases, and with how many elements are those factors associated (sampayutta)?
There is none.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
They are dissociated from one base and from one element by some [factors].
Those phenomena that are associated with the faculty of pleasure … those phenomena that are associated with the faculty of pain …
Those phenomena associated with the faculty of mental joy (somanassindriya),
and those phenomena associated with the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya)— which are included by way of the aggregate-inclusion, the base-inclusion, and the element-inclusion—
[are] associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
They are associated with one base and one element.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
They are dissociated from one base and from one element by some [factors].
Those phenomena which, by way of the inclusion of aggregates, are included by the equanimity faculty, and are included by the inclusion of bases and included by the inclusion of elements—
those phenomena are associated with three aggregates, with one base, and with two elements.
They are associated with one base (āyatana) and one element (dhātu).
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate (khandha), ten bases, and fifteen elements.
They are dissociated from one base (*āyatana*) and from one element (*dhātu*),
and from certain [other] factors. Those factors associated with the faculty of faith (*saddhindriya*) … those factors associated with the faculty of energy (*vīriyindriya*) … [and so on].
Those phenomena associated with the faculty of mindfulness … those phenomena associated with the faculty of concentration … those phenomena associated with the faculty of wisdom …
Those phenomena [associated] with the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," those phenomena [associated] with the faculty of final knowledge,
and those phenomena [associated] with the faculty of one who has already known.
Those phenomena that arise from ignorance… those phenomena that arise from volitional formations conditioned by ignorance… those phenomena that arise from contact conditioned by the six sense bases…
Those phenomena which, conditioned by feeling, are associated with craving;
those phenomena which, conditioned by craving, are associated with clinging;

and those phenomena which, through kamma-becoming, are included in the aggregate-inclusion, included in the base-inclusion, and included in the element-inclusion—those phenomena are associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
With one aggregate, one base, and one element, they are associated with some [factors].
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
They are dissociated from one base and one element.

Regarding those states which, by way of lamentation, are included in the aggregate-inclusion, included in the base-inclusion, and included in the element-inclusion: with how many aggregates, with how many bases, and with how many elements are those states associated?
There are none.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element with respect to some [factors].
Those phenomena which are included by contact,
those phenomena which are included by suffering,

and those phenomena which are included by mental grief— these are included by the classification of aggregates, included by the classification of bases, and included by the classification of elements.
Those states are associated with three aggregates (khandha), one base (āyatana), and seven elements (dhātu);
they are associated with one base and one element by some [factors].
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
they are dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
Those phenomena which [are associated] with despair...
The qualities that are [developed] by means of the foundations of mindfulness...
the qualities that are [developed] by means of the right efforts...
the qualities that are [developed] by means of the immeasurables...
Those phenomena [associated] with the five faculties… those phenomena [associated] with the five powers… those phenomena [associated] with the seven factors of enlightenment…
Those phenomena [associated] with the noble eightfold path;
those phenomena [associated] with contact;
those phenomena [associated] with volition.
Those phenomena which [arise] through resolve;
those phenomena which [arise] through attention;
those phenomena which [arise] through causes.
Those phenomena which [arise] by way of roots and phenomena that possess roots...
those phenomena which [arise] by way of roots and phenomena associated with roots...
those phenomena which [arise] by way of the taints (āsava)...
Those phenomena which [arise] through the taints and through phenomena that are subject to the taints...
those phenomena which [arise] through the taints and through phenomena associated with the taints...
those phenomena which [arise] through the fetters...
Those phenomena that [are included] by way of the categories of phenomena;
those phenomena that [are included] by way of the floods;
those phenomena that [are included] by way of the yokes.
Those phenomena which [arise] from the phenomena of the hindrances;
those phenomena which [arise] from the phenomena of the perversions;
those phenomena which [arise] from the phenomena of clinging.
Those phenomena which [arise] with defiled phenomena;
those phenomena which [arise] with both defiled and contaminating phenomena;
those phenomena which [arise] with both defiled and defiled phenomena.
Regarding those states which, together with the defilements and the states associated with the defilements, are included in the aggregate-grouping,
included in the base-grouping, and included in the element-grouping— by how many aggregates, by how many bases,
and by how many elements are those states associated?
Those states are associated with three aggregates (khandha), one base (āyatana), and seven elements (dhātu);
they are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element by some [factors].
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
they are dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
Two truths and fifteen faculties.
There are eleven dependent terms;
again, there are eleven above;
thus, the "cluster term" here is thirtyfold. [69]
The eleventh chapter: The Exposition of Terms Concerning the Associated and the Dissociated, under the heading of "Included."
